teachingQuestion: What turns a certificate into an operational trust decision?
focalInsight: Enrollment, protected key custody, issuance, relying-party validation, monitoring, rotation or revocation, and recovery each need authority and evidence.
title: PKI is a lifecycle of identity-to-key trust
caption: A certificate's cryptographic signature is one link; the full lifecycle establishes whether it can be relied upon.
altSummary: PKI begins with authorized enrollment and protected key custody, then issuance and relying-party validation; inventory and monitoring support rotation, revocation, recovery, and destruction.
textFallback: Authorize and verify enrollment before binding identity to a key. Protect private keys with scoped custody. Issue certificates under defined policy. At use, validate trust anchor, intended name or identity, validity period, and available status. Inventory dependencies and expiries. Rotate or revoke after expiry, compromise, or material change. Use authorized recovery or destroy material when it is no longer retained.
